e8a08bd8cb.q: What makes Ignition unique compared to other SCADA and HMI platforms in industrial automation?
e8a08bd8cb.a: Dylan highlights that Ignition's user-first design and ease of use set it apart. He explains that with Ignition, when he wanted to accomplish something, the platform provided direct solutions without requiring workarounds or hacks. He particularly praised Ignition for allowing consistent UI design elements like button borders by default, whereas competing SCADA platforms at the time lacked these options, making it difficult to create clean, consistent interfaces. He emphasizes that even early Ignition versions, before object components were available, required less complex scripting than legacy platforms to achieve the same results.
e8a08bd8cb.e: Architecture First: Dylan DuFresne on Digital Infrastructure, UNS, and Building Transformation That Lasts

dc7116cbd6.q: How should manufacturers approach digital transformation instead of chasing buzzwords like Industry 4.0 and UNS?
dc7116cbd6.a: Dylan emphasizes starting with root cause analysis and the five whys framework before any technical implementation. He stresses that digital transformation means different things to different people, and the first step is understanding what business outcome the organization actually wants—whether that is optimizing for sales, quality, margins, or something else. He cautions that sometimes customers pursue digital transformation because the board is asking for it rather than addressing a real business need, and sometimes the answer is as simple as an Excel spreadsheet with good processes rather than new software. The key is identifying what…
dc7116cbd6.e: Architecture First: Dylan DuFresne on Digital Infrastructure, UNS, and Building Transformation That Lasts

50918f9b27.q: What is Abelera's unique approach to Unified Namespace (UNS) implementation in manufacturing?
50918f9b27.a: Dylan explains that most customers pursuing UNS are actually seeking vendor consolidation, as many organizations work with 40 to 50 vendors and need to reduce point-to-point integrations. He identifies two extremes: organizations that are too decentralized with 50-100 platforms and those that are overly centralized with one or two vendors. Abelera's approach is finding a middle ground of four to six platforms connected through a broker with standard naming conventions and topic structures. Dylan emphasizes that a UNS broker is a good starting point but not the end, as it does not eliminate all point-to-point integrations and leaves…
50918f9b27.e: Architecture First: Dylan DuFresne on Digital Infrastructure, UNS, and Building Transformation That Lasts

1f0e5ad947.q: Why is stepwise modernization and internal ownership better than full rip-and-replace digital transformation?
1f0e5ad947.a: Dylan warns that the riskiest thing for a business is outsourcing ownership and accountability to external parties, even well-meaning integrators. He argues that if an organization cannot maintain its systems, it cannot own them, and without ownership it cannot hold anyone accountable. He emphasizes that having the tool an organization can own and maintain is more important than having the best tool. For example, keeping a legacy historian costing seven figures annually might make sense if the team knows how to manage it, whereas switching to an open-source time series database would require new technical headcount and skill sets. Brownfield…
1f0e5ad947.e: Architecture First: Dylan DuFresne on Digital Infrastructure, UNS, and Building Transformation That Lasts

4d1d647171.q: What is Abelera's philosophy for bridging IT strategy and OT execution in manufacturing?
4d1d647171.a: Dylan explains that Abelera bridges strategy and execution by working with IT leadership to understand broader business objectives first—asking questions like where the business is going, what the North Star is, and what the organization is optimizing for. Once business strategy is aligned, technical decisions from choosing which PLC tags to integrate, to whether data goes to cloud or on-site, are all tied back to business objectives and KPIs. This ensures that the solution chosen may not always be the technically perfect choice but is optimized for the business strategy. He notes that working with leadership from the CEO and CFO level down…
4d1d647171.e: Architecture First: Dylan DuFresne on Digital Infrastructure, UNS, and Building Transformation That Lasts

1062ca1eec.q: Who should be the primary stakeholders when designing digital infrastructure for manufacturers?
1062ca1eec.a: Dylan states that successful engagements typically begin with a VP or Director of IT, sometimes a CTO or CIO, and requires a two-directional approach. Rather than a purely top-down approach from IT or bottom-up from the plant floor, Dylan maintains that neither works at scale and a combination of both, meeting in the middle, is necessary. Starting from the IT director level, Abelera then extends conversations upward to the CEO, CFO, CTO, and Director of HR to understand full business strategy, and also coordinates with plant-floor operations teams to understand practical constraints and capabilities.
1062ca1eec.e: Architecture First: Dylan DuFresne on Digital Infrastructure, UNS, and Building Transformation That Lasts

da13d1438e.q: What is batch processing in manufacturing and why is getting it wrong so costly?
da13d1438e.a: Batch processing in industrial manufacturing works like a baking analogy: you follow a recipe with known quantities and process steps to turn raw materials into end product with automated process controls and digital recordation. When mistakes occur in batch processing, manufacturers lose not only raw material costs but also the expensive hazmat disposal and time spent mixing. Industries that depend on batch processing include chemical processors, food and beverage, pharmaceuticals, and construction materials.
da13d1438e.e: Batch, Built Right: How Open Platforms Are Rewriting the Rules of Manufacturing Execution

55145ebd5b.q: How does an open platform approach built on Ignition differ from proprietary batch and MES systems?
55145ebd5b.a: With an open platform like Ignition, solution providers can pick and choose the best technologies to deliver robust solutions and expand capability over time. Proprietary systems create proprietary data silos and are locked in old mentalities and methods that are hard to transfer to younger people. Open platforms allow information created from batch systems to be published in standard format so people can act on issues quicker in real time, enabling tighter tolerances and modern approaches that people understand how to use.
55145ebd5b.e: Batch, Built Right: How Open Platforms Are Rewriting the Rules of Manufacturing Execution

6e8717bee9.q: What is ISA-88 and how does it apply to batch control systems?
6e8717bee9.a: ISA-88 is the gold standard for batch control and is a key standard that allows manufacturers to create standardized approaches. The approach uses standard control modules built in PLC logic that tie through standard interfaces into HMI components and historians. This allows separate components to tie together cleanly, with equipment modules that are standardized and can be deployed rapidly to multiple sites, facilities, and lines with a standard approach to recipe management and control logic.
6e8717bee9.e: Batch, Built Right: How Open Platforms Are Rewriting the Rules of Manufacturing Execution

ef8247c263.q: How did Polaris Automation help PPG Industries move away from Excel-based scheduling?
ef8247c263.a: Polaris built a Core Data scheduling module within Ignition that replicated the same functionality as PPG's Excel-based scheduling that was fed from their ERP exports. After iteratively adding more capability as requested, PPG officially went off Excel completely two weeks before the podcast was recorded and now utilizes the scheduler purely within the platform. This transformation took approximately five years in the making with a cross-functional team approach.
ef8247c263.e: Batch, Built Right: How Open Platforms Are Rewriting the Rules of Manufacturing Execution

5379791195.q: What is the tier board operations approach and how does PPG use it for Kaizen?
5379791195.a: Tier board operations are a true data empowerment technology where PPG operates across tier basis one through five, with operations gathered around tier boards that execute meetings conducted at the same day, time, starting on time and ending on time with the same flow every time. Information ingested through these meetings gets fed into the system and can be used in their Kaizen operations and processes to solve problems that emerge from those discussions.
5379791195.e: Batch, Built Right: How Open Platforms Are Rewriting the Rules of Manufacturing Execution

eb389d74c1.q: Why did Polaris Automation transition from project-based transactional relationships to long-term strategic partnerships with manufacturers?
eb389d74c1.a: Polaris recognized that historically systems from the 90s and 2000s were not set up to support what manufacturers need in the current day and future. Historically the business model was transactional: clients create scope, companies bid, win projects, execute, then support. Now Polaris sees an opportunity and duty as systems integrators to come alongside customers as innovative partners, helping them get outside of the vacuum they operate under and providing hope and encouragement to create clarity out of industry confusion.
eb389d74c1.e: Batch, Built Right: How Open Platforms Are Rewriting the Rules of Manufacturing Execution

d5464abd1d.q: Why did Steve Heckman create Inductive Automation and Ignition instead of building another SCADA tool?
d5464abd1d.a: Steve Heckman, an integrator at CalMetrics, was frustrated that software licensing costs—for clients, tags, screens, and historical data—consumed 80 percent of project costs, leaving integrators only 20-30 percent profit from their engineering hours. His frustration with this business model led him to invent Ignition from the ground up to mitigate these pain points, including a new pricing model and open-source architecture that would benefit integrators and customers alike.
d5464abd1d.e: Built for the Operator: Julio Velasco on Design, Education, and a Career Shaped by Ignition

90662f1240.q: What is the difference between brownfield and greenfield in industrial manufacturing modernization?
90662f1240.a: A brownfield is an existing factory that has been built and operating for decades with mixed legacy equipment like PLC5, Siemens, Mitsubishi, and Omron controllers. A greenfield is a brand new installation with everything built from scratch. Brownfield facilities must evolve incrementally by acknowledging their diverse OEM equipment and integrating them through data concentrators, whereas greenfield projects like new data centers can implement fresh technology from the start.
90662f1240.e: Built for the Operator: Julio Velasco on Design, Education, and a Career Shaped by Ignition

9c333edd01.q: Why is automation considered recession-proof in manufacturing?
9c333edd01.a: During economic expansions, companies invest in automation to grow plants and add new product lines. During economic downturns, they automate to eliminate the most expensive cost—labor—and reduce downtime. Automation performs well in both scenarios: it enables growth during good times and replaces expensive manual labor during recessions, making it fundamentally resistant to economic cycles.
9c333edd01.e: Built for the Operator: Julio Velasco on Design, Education, and a Career Shaped by Ignition

eb86d92850.q: What is the problem with Industry 4.0 implementations that only add sensors and screens to legacy machines?
eb86d92850.a: Many facilities hire new operations managers who call integrators to bolt sensors on machines and add a display screen showing production counts, claiming this achieves Industry 4.0 while the underlying machines still run on PLC5s and micrologics. This approach provides a quick win to justify a new position without addressing the real problem: outdated infrastructure, legacy protocols, and lack of foundational discipline. These operations want immediate gratification without doing the hard work of infrastructure modernization.
eb86d92850.e: Built for the Operator: Julio Velasco on Design, Education, and a Career Shaped by Ignition

b98bce8eca.q: What is the first step Julio Velasco takes when assessing a manufacturing facility for digital transformation?
b98bce8eca.a: Julio starts with a comprehensive audit of both physical hardware and software asset management on a scalable basis—whether one line, one area, or the entire facility. He collects firmware information from PLCs, identifies industrial communication protocols in use like DH45, and documents what devices are connected versus isolated from networks, building a complete picture before recommending any changes.
b98bce8eca.e: Built for the Operator: Julio Velasco on Design, Education, and a Career Shaped by Ignition

2c51dc0307.q: How does modernizing from serial-based protocols like DH45 to Ethernet-based communication improve factory infrastructure?
2c51dc0307.a: Moving from RS-485 serial communication (DH45) to Ethernet requires adding network infrastructure like switches and IDFs, involving electricians and network specialists to run Ethernet drops to edge devices. This is expensive and provides no immediate gratification, but it establishes the foundation needed to connect previously isolated devices, maintain system functionality during the migration, and enable future smart factory capabilities beyond just adding screens.
2c51dc0307.e: Built for the Operator: Julio Velasco on Design, Education, and a Career Shaped by Ignition

cb84bd47da.q: How does FactoryStack manage cloud-first Ignition infrastructure across hundreds of industrial sites?
cb84bd47da.a: FactoryStack manages infrastructure through a central management plane containing declarative code, telemetry, alerting and monitoring, connected to deployment pipelines across customer tenants or 4IR-hosted endpoints. For a customer with 200 facilities, the architecture runs hundreds of databases and Ignition gateways in their Azure tenant, with each site containing an Ignition Edge node collecting data from controllers and OPC servers via MQTT Sparkplug, transmitting to central cloud instances.
cb84bd47da.e: How 4IR Runs Cloud-First Industrial Infrastructure Across Hundreds of Sites

bf2e278ee2.q: What data loss prevention methods does 4IR use when cloud connectivity drops in hybrid Ignition deployments?
bf2e278ee2.a: 4IR uses Ignition Edge, store-and-forward capabilities, and MQTT Sparkplug specifically because of its ability to handle store-and-forward, ensuring data is not lost when Internet connection, SD-WAN or other infrastructure between cloud and facility experiences outages or issues.
bf2e278ee2.e: How 4IR Runs Cloud-First Industrial Infrastructure Across Hundreds of Sites

dda3273ab7.q: How does 4IR enable rapid Ignition infrastructure scaling using infrastructure as code and Kubernetes?
dda3273ab7.a: 4IR uses Kubernetes as a declarative infrastructure-as-code system to deploy and manage Ignition environments at scale. Spinning up new services, databases, or gateways involves making code changes and pushing them to the environment, allowing the infrastructure-as-code tool to match the definition to the system. Multiple non-production and production environments enable regression testing before production deployment.
dda3273ab7.e: How 4IR Runs Cloud-First Industrial Infrastructure Across Hundreds of Sites

1419a5fcb2.q: What observability capabilities does 4IR use to proactively detect Ignition system issues before customers notice them?
1419a5fcb2.a: 4IR captures hundreds of thousands of data points from operated systems and uses synthetic probes to check externally whether applications respond on expected ports, allowing identification of whether problems are infrastructure-related or network-related. Based on years of operational experience, 4IR determines what alerts to trigger and when to act, often fixing issues before customers detect problems.
1419a5fcb2.e: How 4IR Runs Cloud-First Industrial Infrastructure Across Hundreds of Sites

6a49ef2375.q: How does 4IR manage Ignition development and production environment separation to prevent citizen developer changes from impacting operations?
6a49ef2375.a: 4IR implements different security models for production versus development systems, granting appropriate access while maintaining sandbox environments that give developers connectivity they need without affecting production. Pre-negotiating boundaries and understanding security models supports the balance between experimentation and operational stability.
6a49ef2375.e: How 4IR Runs Cloud-First Industrial Infrastructure Across Hundreds of Sites

753346af43.q: What on-premises Kubernetes deployment option has 4IR developed as an alternative to cloud-only Ignition infrastructure?
753346af43.a: In the last year and a half, 4IR built a full on-premises Kubernetes-based high availability deployment capability designed to mimic cloud capabilities including composable architectures, multi-node high availability, automated deployment pipelines, and automated telemetry and observability, with nodes running within facility walls for hybrid cloud deployments.
753346af43.e: How 4IR Runs Cloud-First Industrial Infrastructure Across Hundreds of Sites

4ba7e4d6de.q: What is Factory Brain and how does it differ from traditional unified namespace implementations in manufacturing?
4ba7e4d6de.a: Factory Brain applies a knowledge graph on top of the unified namespace to create relationships between data points. While the UNS gave us an analytics engine to answer questions we know we need to ask, the Factory Brain starts to answer questions we didn't even know we need to ask, moving us from analytics to intelligence. It builds relationships between production events, materials, maintenance, work orders, supply chain, and operators.
4ba7e4d6de.e: The Factory Brain: Remus Pop on Connectivity, Knowledge Graphs, and the Next Era of Operational Intelligence

9d86f4c895.q: How does the Model Context Protocol enable AI agents to automate manufacturing operations beyond predictive alerts?
9d86f4c895.a: MCP essentially gives the ability of a platform or tool access into very detailed information from source systems. Instead of creating point-to-point API integrations, you can now point MCP directly into systems like Ignition to build dashboards through natural language. More importantly, in the agentic world, agents interact with software tools through MCP, enabling automated workflows like adjusting production schedules, reserving maintenance parts, and creating work orders automatically when predictive maintenance alerts occur.
9d86f4c895.e: The Factory Brain: Remus Pop on Connectivity, Knowledge Graphs, and the Next Era of Operational Intelligence

e05487e249.q: Why should manufacturers build data infrastructure first rather than committing to specific AI platforms and tools?
e05487e249.a: The software landscape is being completely transformed by AI, and new foundational models from companies like Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google can kill 500 different SaaS offerings overnight. By abstracting the platform away from infrastructure, manufacturers protect their investment and avoid situations where they invested time and money in a pilot only to have a new model emerge that makes their entire investment a complete waste. The approach is to plug data into infrastructure, not into applications.
e05487e249.e: The Factory Brain: Remus Pop on Connectivity, Knowledge Graphs, and the Next Era of Operational Intelligence

ddce014052.q: How does the concept of the nervous system apply to Ignition in factory automation architecture?
ddce014052.a: Ignition functions as the nervous system of the factory, not just a connectivity or visualization tool. It must be an engine of data that flows information into an endpoint that drives intelligence. The nervous system's goal is to feed everything in motion with context to what needs it. Ignition has the ability to connect to many different things inside a factory and serves as that data river and context engine that feeds every part of the system with the data needed to drive value.
ddce014052.e: The Factory Brain: Remus Pop on Connectivity, Knowledge Graphs, and the Next Era of Operational Intelligence

d26670f29d.q: What was Remus Pop's experience deploying Ignition across Dana's manufacturing footprint?
d26670f29d.a: Remus Pop's team won a Firebrand Award with Ignition at Dana, where his job was to roll Ignition out to all 100+ factories. This extensive deployment across multiple facilities gave him deep insight into IT-OT convergence and identified a market gap where there were integration specialists who understood the shop floor and others who understood IT landscape, but very few who knew both and could operate in the middle ground of IT-OT convergence.
d26670f29d.e: The Factory Brain: Remus Pop on Connectivity, Knowledge Graphs, and the Next Era of Operational Intelligence

8375a84dc0.q: How does knowledge graph prevent staleness and maintain real-time relationships in manufacturing systems?
8375a84dc0.a: A knowledge graph can become stale because it represents a point-in-time snapshot when it was built, and manufacturing environments change daily. However, when you create MCP interactions with systems like Ignition, the knowledge graph doesn't become stale anymore because you can constantly be aware of what's changing in Ignition through that MCP. The same principle applies to interactions with external systems, maintaining live context.
8375a84dc0.e: The Factory Brain: Remus Pop on Connectivity, Knowledge Graphs, and the Next Era of Operational Intelligence
